To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a centrally mounted spark plug allows a substantial reduction of CO emissions in a bio syngas fueled spark ignition engine, while maintaining a high efficiency and a good power level.

a) the spark plug position has a relevant effect on the combustion process, especially on the CO emission; b) the spark position and the mixture ratio are the main parameters to be tuned in a bio syngas SI engine in order to reduce CO emissions without affecting engine performances; c) the use of an alternative bio syngas as a fuel for a SI engine is a valid alternative for the reduction of the environmental impact of the engine.

a central mounted spark, alongwith a correct calibration of mixture ratio and Start of Spark, allows a reduction in CO emissions of more than 95% with respect to the reference condition without penalizing engine efficiency and brake power.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of the engine geometry and the operating conditions in order to reduce the environmental impact and to improve the combustion efficiency of a syngas SI engine.
the optimization of the combustion chamber geometry of a syngas SI engine in order to increase the engine efficiency and reduce the environmental impact.
the optimization of a SI engine powered with syngas from a biomass gasification process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the numerical models developed by authors can be considered a reliable tool to predict the combustion process occurring in a SI syngas engine and to support the design of a new generation of alternative engines.
a proper optimization of the engine geometry can lead to a substantial improvement of the combustion efficiency, thus reducing the environmental impact of a syngas powered SI engine.

the proposed numerical analysis, based on a 3D CFD approach coupled to a chemical reaction mechanism and to a 1D model for the prediction of the engine performance, allows the optimization of the combustion chamber geometry and the engine operating conditions, in terms of mixture ratio and ignition timing, to improve its performance and reduce its environmental impact, with respect to a standard SI engine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the numerical models developed by authors can be successfully employed to predict the effects of different engine configurations on the engine performances and on the exhaust gas emissions, and to optimize them with respect to the desired targets.

the use of a centrally mounted spark plug in an SI engine powered by syngas from gasification is a valid alternative to the traditional spark position in order to improve the combustion efficiency and reduce the CO emissions.
the optimization of the spark plug position and the mixture air-to-fuel ratio can lead to a significant decrease of CO emissions in a bio syngas SI engine, without affecting its efficiency and power.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the spark location and the timing of the ignition have a strong influence on engine performance and emissions, and that the optimization of the engine combustion cycle is a complex task that needs to be addressed by means of a multidisciplinary approach.
the numerical approach is a valuable tool for the development of a syngas SI engine, especially for the design of the combustion chamber geometry and the calibration of the engine parameters.

the optimization of the spark plug position is a crucial factor in order to obtain the highest combustion efficiency in a syngas SI engine, and that the developed models are a valid support for the design of the engine geometry.
